summary.headline: Aurionpro Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.3% YoY to Rs 358 crore, EBITDA margin about 17%, with management declining full-year guidance.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 358 crore, up 6.3% YoY, with Banking and FinTech up about 5% to over Rs 200 crore and TIG up 8.4% to Rs 157 crore. EBITDA was Rs 61 crore (about 17% margin) and PAT was Rs 45 crore. Management attributed the below-trajectory quarter to MEA disruption, project go-live timing, data center milestones, supply chain pressure and capacity diverted to banking product build-outs. Management said demand is not the issue, pointed to a record 23 new logos and the largest-ever US order, and declined to give full-year revenue or margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +8.4% YoY; sequential decline per analyst question
expected to remain similar this year

segments.name: Banking and FinTech
segments.commentary: Revenue above Rs 200 crore, up about 5% YoY. Large share of capacity diverted to banking product build-outs (transaction banking, trade finance), which management said depresses near-term revenue and margin; expected to normalise over one to two quarters.

segments.name: TIG (Transit, Infrastructure, Governance)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 157 crore, up 8.4% YoY, but down sequentially. Data center is about one-third of TIG; management expects it to rise to about 40% of TIG by year-end with 50-100% growth. Data center margin is 4-5 points below enterprise margin.

segments.name: Data center
segments.commentary: Execution started on one of the largest projects; management expects Q2 pickup and more significant acceleration in Q3 and Q4. Growth had run at 40-50%, now expected to exceed that. Not disclosed separately.

guidance_outlook: No full-year revenue or margin guidance; management said too many uncertain factors.
Management expects acceleration through the year, mainly in H2, citing H2 typically larger than H1 and large project execution in Q3-Q4.
Banking to stay a few points above 50% of mix and TIG a few points below 50% for FY27; mix shift more likely next year.
Middle East impact expected to be gone by Q3 on a year-on-year basis; some Middle East wins hoped for in the next one to two quarters.
Operating cash flow: H1 likely negative or close to zero; management intends to show progress through the year and will update at mid-H1.
No significant acquisitions planned for the next few quarters; R&D expense not to increase meaningfully.
capex_capacity: Capacity is being built in advance for data center demand, which is currently weighing on the cost structure.
Banking capacity diverted to product build-outs (transaction banking, trade finance, AI-native stack); management expects this to normalise over one to two quarters.
Data center business consumes very little capital, according to management.
Workforce expansion is being paced gradually; management said there is no fundamental capacity shortfall and productivity gains from AI tools will offset some capacity diversion.
Management described the business as about 13-14 P&Ls, mostly product P&Ls.
demand_pricing: Record 23 new customer logos in Q1; largest-ever US order; a large transaction banking mandate; Mumbai Metro and Delhi Metro transit mandates.
Order book described as strong and pipeline as the busiest management has seen; management said it would not discuss deals before closing.
Middle East revenue fell to zero from double-digit share last year; management said it lacks a good handle on the timing of recovery.
Transaction banking win rates upwards of 50% on products once built out, per management.
Management said conversion is slowed by long project duration (large deals versus typical 12-month projects) and capacity ramp-up needs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TIG decline sequentially despite data center execution starting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the large data center deal takes time to ramp; Q2 will see a pickup and Q3 and Q4 a more significant one.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin drop given banking grew faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin fell due to revenue, business mix and capacity converting order book to revenue; R&D expensed on product build-outs temporarily lowers EBITDA. Banking margins expected to strengthen over three to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company provide full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it sees acceleration through the year, especially H2, but will not give revenue or margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Data center margin and full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Data center margin is four to five points below enterprise margin for now; management expects volume to offset this and margins to improve over a multi-year period.

qa_highlights.question: Will data center be disclosed as a separate segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider sub-segment disclosure internally, without commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 cash conversion target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 operating cash flow is likely negative or close to zero due to payment cycles; progress expected in H2 with an update at mid-H1.

risks_watch: Middle East: no deal closures yet; revenue from the region fell to zero from double-digit share last year.

Execution: sequential TIG decline and conversion below normal trajectory; H2 acceleration depends on large projects keeping to schedule, with management warning that a slip from Q4 to Q1 could be material.
Margin: EBITDA margin about 17% versus a 20-22% earlier reference; R&D at about 10.5-11% and data center mix are headwinds.
Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow likely negative; management to update at mid-H1.
Employee cost growth versus flat-to-slow revenue growth, as raised by an analyst; management attributes this to capacity build and productivity gains.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic but evasive on forward numbers: management declined full-year guidance and sub-segment disclosure, and repeatedly deferred H2 acceleration claims. It was candid about execution shortfalls in the Middle East, banking conversion and capacity.
key_quotes: This is not really a demand issue. Our order book is strong. The pipeline is healthy.
I don't want to get into giving guidance right now. I don't think we can do a very accurate job at it right now.

adds.what: Data center capacity being built in advance for demand (no size or capex disclosed)

growth.why: Management declined full-year revenue guidance but expects acceleration through the year mainly in H2, with data center growth now expected above its 40-50% run-rate and a record 23 logos and strong order book, though Q1 revenue grew only 6.3% YoY and H1 operating cash flow is guided near zero.
